speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative check-up. To better understand your shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty, I need to ask: When did these symptoms start relative to your surgery, and is the pain sharp or dull? Do you notice any fluid drainage, fever, or hearing changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the shooting pain upon chewing and discomfort with earrings are concerning signs after your right ear tympanoplasty. Given your history of chronic ear infections, have you noticed any fluid drainage, fever, or a change in hearing since your surgery? Also, do you have any visible redness or swelling at the eardrum perforation site?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pain when eating and discomfort with earrings suggests a tethered tympanic membrane or persistent scarring affecting your ear canal and eardrum movement. Have you noticed any changes in hearing, dizziness, or visible scarring in the ear canal since your surgery? REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy with microscopic examination.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Otoscopy with microscopic examination reveals a smooth, glistening tympanic membrane with no visible scarring, retraction pockets, or active infection. The ear canal is clear of debris. However, upon palpation, slight tenderness is noted at the postauricular area correlating with the right tonsillar region, while the preauricular and mandibular areas remain non-tender. Hearing remains stable with no reported dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tethered Tympanic Membrane (Glue Ear Syndrome/Myositis Ossificans variant). The normal otoscopy rules out active infection or scarring, but the specific combination of post-tympanoplasty shooting pain triggered by jaw movement (eating) and discomfort with earrings, despite a clear canal, is highly suggestive of a tethered membrane causing micro-movements during chewing. The tenderness near the tonsillar region may indicate referred pain or adjacent muscle involvement, but the primary ear pathology is the tethering.
